logline: High-school delinquent Tomoya Okazaki meets girl after girl with quiet sorrows in his final year - then the story follows him into adulthood, marriage, and grief, in one of anime's most emotionally demanding coming-of-age sagas.

renewal.note: Both cours - Clannad (2007-2008) and Clannad: After Story (2008-2009) - completed their run. No sequel series has been produced. The source visual novel by Key/Visual Art's remains the definitive version of the story.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.2 across both cours reflects audience affection, but season 1 functions as an extended prologue - praised for Kyoto Animation's craft yet critically considered thinner than After Story.

seasons.review_body: Kyoto Animation adapted Key's beloved visual novel across the TBS and MBS networks starting October 2007. Season 1 is a high-school arc that introduces Tomoya Okazaki and a set of girls with individual routes drawn directly from the visual novel structure, where each girl's backstory gets 2-4 episodes of careful emotional payoff. Kyoto Animation's production quality stands out through fluid character animation, expressive faces, and a score by Yoshino Natsume and Maeda Jun. The route-based, episodic structure also gives Season 1 the feel of a deliberate warm-up, rather than a purely standalone story. The IMDb combined series rating of 8.2 sits a full point below After Story's isolated score, aligning with that overall assessment.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb 8.8 and a MAL weighted score of 9.01 place After Story among the highest-rated anime series in recorded history; critics at Anime News Network called it an 'exploration of adult life that most romance anime gloss over'.

pull_quotes.text: The last two-thirds of After Story offer some of the most heartbreaking and authentic explorations of everyday adulthood pains.

seasons.review_body: Clannad: After Story is a deeply emotionally devastating second season. Where season 1 builds its narrative around school drama, After Story drops the multi-route structure to follow Tomoya and Nagisa from marriage into parenthood and profound loss. The weighted score of 9.01 places it among the all-time top anime, and the IMDb audience score of 8.8 reflects strong viewer approval. The final act is framed as heartbreaking and authentic in its depiction of adult grief. Kyoto Animation allows tragedy to linger without resolution for multiple episodes, a structural patience that stands out from typical anime pacing. The ending turns to a visual novel mechanic to offer a form of reprieve, which creates contrasting reactions to whether it complements or weakens the grief established earlier.
seasons.season_over_season: Abandons the episodic route structure entirely for a sustained life-arc that takes the show from teenage romance to adult bereavement - a tonal leap few anime attempt.

episode_reviews.title: The Ends of the Earth
episode_reviews.review_body: Clannad: After Story Episode 18 is the episode the entire series had been building toward and the reason After Story holds a MAL weighted score of 9.01 from over 600,000 voters - a figure that places it in the small tier of anime whose emotional investment was definitively paid out in a single hour. The episode arrives at Tomoya’s arc at its lowest point: the full weight of what the series has been about, the themes of family and responsibility and the cost of ordinary adult life, land here without mitigation or consolation. Kyoto Animation’s direction of the hospital sequences and the aftermath - Tomoya’s silence, the walk away from the building - executes the emotional statement with the restraint that makes it devastating rather than manipulative. Anime News Network’s review of After Story called this arc ‘some of the most heartbreaking and authentic explorations of everyday adulthood pains’ in anime; Episode 18 is the apex of that assessment.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: After Story’s emotional apex arrives in the episode where Tomoya’s arc reaches its lowest point, when the full weight of the series’ themes lands without mitigation. The episode carries such emotional force that it stands out as the one most likely to bring viewers to tears.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Tomoya walks away from the hospital in silence. What he has lost and what it costs him is written entirely in that walk.
